solution: Change the division to multiplication by the reciprocal, that is, flip the second fraction: $\frac{x^2+{=p+q}x+{=p*q}}{{=c}(x^2-{=q*q})}\times\frac{{=n}x^2-{=n*q}x}{{=d}x^2+{=d*p}x}$
Factorise every numerator and denominator: $x^2+{=p+q}x+{=p*q}=(x+{=p})(x+{=q})$, $x^2-{=q*q}=(x-{=q})(x+{=q})$, ${=d}x^2+{=d*p}x={=d}x(x+{=p})$ and ${=n}x^2-{=n*q}x={=n}x(x-{=q})$
Write the product with every factor showing: $\frac{(x+{=p})(x+{=q})}{{=c}(x-{=q})(x+{=q})}\times\frac{{=n}x(x-{=q})}{{=d}x(x+{=p})}$
notes:
Parametrises the book's most repeated exercise (ex1-10-2a/b/c, ex1-11-31f/j; ex1-11-31e has the same skeleton). Skeleton: (x+p)(x+q) / [c(x-q)(x+q)] divided by d*x(x+p) / [n*x(x-q)], with n = r*c*d so the result n/(c*d) = r is a whole number by construction, exactly as in the book (answers 5, 3, 4, 2, 5, 5). The trinomial is written in expanded form x^2+(p+q)x+pq and the student must factorise it; p != q so the trinomial is not a perfect square. Ranges chosen to match the book's magnitudes: q 2..11, p 2..12, largest coefficient n*q <= 100*11 = 1100, as in ex1-11-31j (100d^2-1100d). Verified by exact rational evaluation at several x over all 4800 parameter combinations (answer r, never depends on x). The variable letter is fixed at x (the book varies it; the answer is a number so nothing is lost).
